wins.text: CIB revenue grew 26% year-over-year; markets revenue increased 33% YoY driven by structured products, equities, credit products and commodities; banking revenue up 15% YoY
Repurchased $12 billion of common stock in 2023; CET1 ratio at 11.4%, 2.5 percentage points above regulatory minimum; expects to repurchase more than $12B in 2024
Credit card new account growth up 17% YoY; credit card spend up 15% for the year; card balances up 40% since end of 2021
Full-year 2023 NII of $52.4 billion, reflecting strong growth vs. 2022; expenses declined YoY driven by lower operating losses and efficiency initiatives delivering ~$10B gross savings since 2020
Mobile active customers grew by 1.6 million in 2023; mobile logins up 11% YoY; 20 million consumer interactions with Fargo AI assistant

risks.text: Full-year 2024 NII guided to be approximately 7%-9% lower than 2023's $52.4B, with NII expected to trough toward year-end; driven by deposit mix shift, lower rates, and modest loan declines

Commercial real estate office net charge-offs increased materially; CRE office nonaccrual loans rose $567M in Q4; management acknowledged 'we're still in the beginning of the movie' on CRE losses, which will be 'uneven and episodic'
Net loan charge-offs rose 17 bps QoQ to 53 bps of average loans; consumer charge-offs at 79 bps driven by maturing credit card vintages; card charge-offs expected to trend higher in 2024
Noninterest-bearing deposits declined to 27% of mix; average deposits down 3% YoY as consumers migrate to higher-yielding alternatives; further consumer deposit attrition expected in 2024

Reported Q4 ROTCE of only 9% (impacted by $1.9B FDIC special assessment and $969M severance); path to 15% ROTCE described as medium-term with no specific timeline given; analysts openly questioned the slow pace of improvement

guidance_items.detail: Full-year 2024 NII expected to be approximately 7%-9% lower than 2023's $52.4B; NII to trough toward end of 2024
NIM expected to compress as NII declines on a relatively stable balance sheet; deposit mix shift and rate cuts are headwinds
2024 noninterest expense guided to approximately $52.6B, down from $53.6B adjusted 2023 base (excluding FDIC special assessment)
Share repurchases expected to exceed $12B done in 2023; CET1 buffer of 2.5 ppts above minimums supports increased buybacks
Ongoing business-related operating losses expected at ~$1.3B in 2024, consistent with 2023 levels

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Pace and timeline for ROTCE improvement from 9% to 15% — analysts pressed management on why ROTCE has barely moved in 3 years
Specific quarterly NII trajectory and Q1 step-down magnitude — management declined to give quarterly guidance
Basel III Endgame and DFAST stress test implications for buyback acceleration timing
